answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the tundra identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator pays for 270 runs and collects one. Because the orchard index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the yarrow audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 270 answers need 270 separate inference runs with separate seeds. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
